title: Senior Software Engineer, Inference Performance
description:
About Tensordyne 

AI is transforming our world. It can perform cognitive functions that previously only humans could do, such as perceiving interactions across different modalities and environments - with the ability to quickly learn and then solve complex problems. Tensordyne is an AI system solution company that builds very high-performance, low-power generative AI inference systems. Our mission, through the creation of custom silicon, hardware and software, is to enable multimodal Generative AI inference acceleration at scale, with safe, sustainable, high-performance systems for our hyperscaler and neocloud data center customers. We are at the leading edge of advancing the latest research and product improvements for generative Al inference solutions that will make Al even more advantageous for compelling new generative AI applications.Tensordyne is a well funded, fast-paced startup company with headquarters in both Sunnyvale, CA, and Munich, Germany. We also have many talented team members working remotely across North America and Europe. We take care of our people and their families with comprehensive benefits, competitive compensation, flexible spending options, and recognition programs, because building category-defining technology starts with a healthy, supported team. Come join us as we shape the future of multimodal generative artificial intelligence!

The role

You’ll build the software stack that takes a model from code down to the hardware: the abstractions, kernels, libraries, and tools that engineers and agents use to reach peak performance. Help optimize the latest AI models on our silicon.

Our hardware is designed to be straightforward to program, so the goal is not to hide it. The goal is to expose the right level of control at each layer, from our compiler-driven Python SDK to our low-level Rust programming stack, and to make every performance gap measurable and every fix permanent.

We’re looking for a builder who understands hardware deeply and develops with agents by default. You’ll own substantial parts of one of these layers and work closely with engineers across models, compilers, runtime, and hardware. Your focus is performance: where cycles, bandwidth, and communication go, and how to win them back. Number formats and model accuracy are owned by our conversion and emulation team; you’ll partner with them where precision and speed meet.

What you’ll do

  • Build the stack. Design APIs, kernel abstractions, and libraries in our Python SDK or Rust stack so model engineers and agents can reach high performance at the layer that fits their problem.
  • Make models fast. Take priority workloads, from LLMs to multimodal models, to peak performance on real silicon. Profile, find the bottleneck across kernels, compiler, runtime, and parallelism, and fix it at the right layer.
  • Close the gap between model and measurement. Compare measured performance against analytical models and simulation. Explain every material gap, and turn the explanation into a fix or a better model.
  • Build the agentic performance loop. Give agents the profilers, traces, counters, and benchmark harnesses to form a hypothesis, change code, and measure the result in minutes. Make the results trustworthy enough to act on.
  • Set the bar for performance. Define how we measure, track regressions, and report results.
  • Build for the next chip. Design abstractions that carry forward to future hardware generations. Work with hardware architects to test how architectural choices affect real workloads.

What we need from you

  • You understand hardware performance. You’ve optimized AI workloads on GPUs or custom accelerators and can reason about compute utilization, memory hierarchy, latency hiding, synchronization, and multi-chip scaling.
  • You build excellent software. You’ve owned substantial systems from design through production. You’re strong in Python and/or at least one systems language such as Rust, C++, or C, and rigorous about interfaces, abstractions, and testing. We care about engineering quality more than a specific language.
  • You understand LLM inference end to end. You can read a new model’s implementation and reason about prefill, decode, attention variants, KV caches, MoE, and parallelism, and how they map to compute, memory, and communication.
  • You build with agents. Agentic development is how you work, not an experiment. You’d rather build the loop that finds the optimization than find it by hand, and you know when the loop still needs a human.
  • You build things others succeed with. You’ve designed APIs, libraries, or performance tooling that other engineers adopted.
  • You drive problems to resolution. You form clear hypotheses, measure, and follow the evidence across software and hardware boundaries. You take ownership of the result.

If you hit a few of those boxes, we’d like to speak to you.

We’d be thrilled if you had

  • Experience with embedded, bare-metal, or low-level runtime programming.
  • Experience with MLIR, other compiler frameworks, or kernel DSLs such as Triton, Pallas, NKI, or CuTe.
  • Contributions to LLM serving stacks such as vLLM or SGLang, or a track record of taking end-to-end inference workloads to competitive performance on a hardware target.

Why join us

Your code will decide how fast models run on our hardware, and how easy it is for the next engineer, or the next agent, to make them faster. You’ll own a layer of a new programming model, work directly with the people designing the hardware, and see your decisions tested on real silicon and carried into the next generation.

Tensordyne Values

  • Think big. Pursue ambitious technical and business goals.
  • Aim for excellence. Quality matters in everything we build and deliver.
  • Own it and get it done. Take responsibility and drive results.
  • Operate with integrity. Be direct, transparent, and respectful.
  • Win as a team. Make the people around you more effective.
  • Value different perspectives. The strongest teams challenge assumptions and bring diverse experience to difficult problems.

Tensordyne is an equal opportunity employer. We believe diverse teams are better equipped to solve complex problems and build exceptional technology. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, color, gender identity or expression, marital status, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, race, religion, pregnancy, sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws, regulations, and ordinances.

About the role

Let's get into the specifics. It’s impossible to capture every nuance of a role – especially at a rapidly growing company like Mews – but if we had to distil it into a job description (which we do because this is a job description), it would be this:

You will own the agents, skills and standards that let a tribe of product builders move quickly on payments without the architecture fragmenting. Hotels take payments across regions and through providers that each behave differently, and Payment Interfaces exists to give customers one coherent payment experience on top of several PSPs. Embedded payments at this depth is rare among European SaaS companies, so the problems here are ones few engineers get to work on.

You will be a Staff Engineer in the Payment Interfaces team, part of the Fintech tribe. You will report to the Director of Product and Engineering, sit in the tribe’s leadership group, and work alongside product builders, other staff engineers and product managers. No one reports to you, so your influence comes from the architecture, tools and standards that other people choose to work in.

The team integrates several PSPs depending on region and conditions. When integrations drift apart, builders slow down and quality suffers. This role exists to keep them coherent by encoding what good looks like into tools and agents, so every builder meets the standard by default.

  • Own the tribe’s engineering agents, skills and context, and encode architectural standards, review logic and quality gates into them so the standard is met by default.
  • Build an AI first responder for customer tickets about payment issues, with clear rules for when it answers and when it hands over to a person.

  • Keep Payment Interfaces integrations coherent as PSPs and regional requirements change, collaborating with builders who own their own work.
  • Coach builders and fix off-standard outcomes at the cause, so the lesson sticks.

AI Fluency Level 4: in this role, that means you build the AI systems the tribe works in, not only use them. You design the agents, skills and evaluations that builders rely on every day, make the engineering decisions about how they behave, and set the rules for when an AI answer can stand and when a person must step in.

  • Hands-on experience integrating with payment service providers or payment processors.
  • Deep engineering craft and architectural judgment, including a sense of what is worth codifying and what is a one-off.
  • AI Fluency Level 4 or the equivalent hands-on experience: you have built agents, skills, evaluations or tooling that other engineers use, and you can explain where human oversight stays non-negotiable.
  • A systems mindset that turns hard-won knowledge into reusable architecture and tooling rather than documentation.
  • Comfort with influence as your main way of getting things done, working with builders, product managers, principals and senior leaders without anyone reporting to you.

Nice to have 

  • Experience in hospitality, travel or another operationally complex B2B SaaS environment.
  • Experience publishing or speaking externally about your work.
  • A track record of coaching other engineers and multiplying their effectiveness.

title: Senior .NET Software Engineer
description:
We're looking for a Senior Software Engineer to design, build, and evolve our enterprise data APIs. This role will be actively involved in API architecture and delivery, contribute to a new API catalog and self-service discovery portal, and help drive AI-assisted improvements to how we design, build, and ship APIs. Experience identifying and fixing security vulnerabilities using SAST tools (e.g., SonarQube), DAST tools, and OWASP-aligned practices. Strong communication skills, with proven experience in cross-team coordination. Experience with requirement analysis, estimation, and deliverable planning. Preferred Qualifications Experience with Druid or Oracle. Exposure to AI/LLM-assisted development workflows. Experience with API catalog/registry or developer portal tooling.
